reigns.note: Aeolid whom Apollodorus makes king over Boeotia; Pausanias settles him on the Athamantian Plain by the Copaic Lake and Mount Laphystius in Orchomenian country — regional power beside the Andreus city-succession, not the Arcadian Orchomenus.
Son of the river Peneius; first settler of the land afterward called Andreis, the opening of Pausanias' Boeotian Orchomenus king-list.
Son of Andreus by Euippe (or, locally, of the Cephisus); kept the land-name Andreis and founded two tribes — not the Theban son of Oedipus.
Son of Ares by Chryse daughter of Almus; took the throne when Eteocles died childless and renamed the country Phlegyantis.
Son of Poseidon by Chrysogeneia daughter of Almus; succeeded the childless Phlegyas and begot Minyas — not Chryses the priest of Apollo at Chryse.
King who built the treasury and begot Orchomenus the eponym; Apollonius makes him son of Aeolus instead (Arg. 3.1077).

Son of Minyas in whose reign the city took its name; the people kept the name Minyans to distinguish them from the Arcadian Orchomenians. Died childless — not the Thyestes-son banquet victim (`orchomenus`), nor Lycaon's Arcadian eponym.
Son of Iasus who once ruled mightily in Orchomenus of the Minyae — Homer's Minyan king and father of Chloris; outside Pausanias' Andreus–Minyas–Clymenus succession, and not the Theban wall-builder.
Son of Presbon son of Phrixus; inherited when Orchomenus died childless. Wounded at Onchestus by a Theban charioteer — the grievance that set Erginus' tribute on Thebes.
Son of Clymenus, who sent heralds to Thebes for the tribute until Heracles routed the Minyans — slain in Apollodorus, spared to rebuild and father Trophonius and Agamedes in Pausanias.
After Trophonius was swallowed in the Lebadeian grove, Pausanias says the kingdom passed to the sons of Ares and Astyoche — the same pair Homer leads to Troy from Orchomenus and Aspledon.
